Bitcoin's rival BIP-110 minority chain stalls after mining only 2 blocks in 8 hours –
Link
The contested BIP-110 "anti-spam" proposal, which sought to restrict certain non-financial uses of Bitcoin block space, entered mandatory signaling with only ≈2.5% miner support. The resulting minority fork produced just two blocks before stalling.
Matters because: this suggests Bitcoin's consensus mechanism remains resistant to contentious protocol changes without broad economic buy-in, reinforcing network stability expectations.

tweet.text:
Last week in Bitcoin:

- Bitcoin held below $65K all week, recovering to ~$65,000 by Aug 8–9, up +3% to +4% on the week as a weak July jobs print offset a hawkish Fed hold. 
- US spot Bitcoin ETFs booked roughly $853M of net inflows on a five-day streak, with BlackRock's IBIT taking 81% ($693M). 
- BitGo's CEO funded a public 100 BTC wallet and dared Anthropic's Claude to drain it; the wallet was untouched as of Aug 10. 
- Strategy (MSTR) kept selling, offloading 1,638 BTC and unveiled a $15B Bitcoin-backed preferred program while lifting its cash reserve target to $4B. 
- Corporate treasuries diverged: SpaceX confirmed it still holds 18,712 BTC and sold none, Block reached 9,117 BTC, while MARA trimmed to 35,577 BTC and pledged 18,750 BTC as loan collateral. 
- BIP-110's rival chain stalled almost immediately, mining just 2 blocks in 8 hours against. 
- Two infrastructure exploits hit the ecosystem (Coldcard, ~$130M; BTCPay Server on LND).
